union.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

land.text: Qui Nhơn (Bình Định) from 1773, the south-central coast from 1775 and Gia Định from 1776-1777

predecessors.note: The Tây Sơn rose against the Nguyễn lord Phúc Thuần in 1771 and took the Nguyễn lords' land piecemeal; the lords' own dossier closes in 1777.

land.text: the northern outline, Đàng Ngoài, taken in 1786-1788

predecessors.note: Thuận Hóa 1786; the Trịnh lords end 1787 and Nguyễn Huệ holds the north from 1788-1789 (Cliopatria shape 1788).

land.text: the northern rump (Thăng Long/Bắc Thành and the north) and the rest of the Tây Sơn lands, taken by Nguyễn Ánh between 1799 and 1802

successors.note: Nguyễn Ánh took Quy Nhơn 1799/1801, Phú Xuân 3 May 1801 and Hanoi on 20 July 1802; the Nguyễn dynasty of Gia Long follows on the whole of Vietnam.

capitals.name: Quy Nhơn (Qui Nhơn), rebel base
capitals.note: Nguyễn Nhạc page: 'Quy Nhơn was taken by Tây Sơn army and used as their new base camp' (undated; the DYN page dates the capture of the port to 1773). The brothers' home village of Tây Sơn is the origin of the name; a formal capital begins in 1776.

capitals.name: Đồ Bàn (Bình Định)
capitals.note: Infobox: Đồ Bàn (1776-1788). Nguyễn Nhạc page: 1776, Nhạc 'titled himself Tây Sơn vương and used Đồ Bàn Citadel as his capital'. After 1788 Nhạc keeps Quy Nhơn as King of Tây Sơn until his death in 1793.

capitals.name: Phú Xuân (Huế)
capitals.note: Infobox: Phú Xuân (1788-1801); Quang Trung is crowned on Bân Hill at Phú Xuân on 22 December 1788 (Quang Trung page). Lost to Nguyễn Ánh on 3 May 1801.

capitals.name: Bắc Thành (Thăng Long, Hanoi)
capitals.note: Infobox: Bắc Thành (1801-1802); Quang Toản 'fled to Thăng Long' after Phú Xuân fell.

rulers.name: Nguyễn Nhạc (Thái Đức)
rulers.title: rebel leader; Tây Sơn vương from 1776; emperor Thái Đức 1778-1788
rulers.note: Infobox gives Thái Đức 1778-1788. Leader of the 1771 revolt with his brothers; titled himself Tây Sơn vương in 1776 and crowned himself emperor in 1778 (Nguyễn Nhạc page); after 1788 he 'resigned as Emperor and declared himself King of Tây Sơn' and held Quy Nhơn until 1793.

rulers.name: Quang Trung (Nguyễn Huệ)
rulers.note: Proclaimed emperor on 22 December 1788; died 16 September 1792 (Quang Trung page).

rulers.name: Cảnh Thịnh (Nguyễn Quang Toản)
rulers.note: Enthroned at age ten in 1792 with his uncle Bùi Đắc Tuyên in real power; captured and executed in 1802.

correction.text: Qui Nhơn, captured by the Tây Sơn in 1773, and the Tây Sơn uplands behind it; before 1773 an upland rebel base only

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Tây Sơn shape begins in 1775, but the page dates the revolt to 1771 ('rose to revolt in 1771 against the Nguyễn lord Phúc Thuần') and the capture of the port of Qui Nhơn to 1773. The page names a village and a port, not a province; Bình Định (Quy Nhơn and the Tây Sơn uplands behind it) is my reading. Infobox: 'Rebel governance (1771-1778)'.

correction.text: Tây Sơn land 1775: the south-central coast from Quảng Nam to Khánh Hòa and the uplands, with Bình Định

keyframe_review.note: 1775 (166 cells, 48,363 km2): Cliopatria draws only Phú Yên, Khánh Hòa and the Central Highlands (Gia Lai, Kon Tum, Đắk Lắk) and leaves out Bình Định, the Tây Sơn core and base since 1773, while its Trịnh lords row (1775-1777) is given Bình Định to Quảng Bình. The Nguyễn Nhạc page has the Tây Sơn take Quảng Nam and 'the country from Quảng Ngãi to Bình Thuận' (no year; I place it after the Trịnh capture of Phú Xuân in February 1775, Trịnh-Nguyễn War page). The correction adds Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Nam and Đà Nẵng; Nhạc then held them as a Trịnh official (the trinh-lords dossier records the vassalage 1775-1778). The Central Highlands are in the Cliopatria shape but no page opened mentions them. Infobox area: none.

correction.text: the 1776 Cliopatria shape plus the Tây Sơn core coast from Bình Định to Đà Nẵng

keyframe_review.note: 1776-1777 (190 cells): adds the Mekong delta around Gia Định ('in 1776 the Tây Sơn army captured the last Nguyễn stronghold of Gia Định'; the Quang Trung page has Huệ and Lữ take Saigon in 1777). The same omission as 1775: Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Nam and Đà Nẵng are missing although Nhạc's capital Đồ Bàn is in Bình Định from 1776 (Nguyễn Nhạc page).

minus.text: Thuận Hóa, the Nguyễn heartland from the Gianh River to the Hải Vân Pass, read as the three modern provinces
Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

correction.text: the Tây Sơn coast from Đà Nẵng and Quảng Nam to Khánh Hòa and the uplands, without the Trịnh province of Thuận Hóa and without Nguyễn Ánh's Gia Định, 1778-1781

keyframe_review.note: 1778-1787 (331 cells, 102,119 km2 = the Nguyễn lords' former area): the shape runs from Quảng Bình to Khánh Hòa and the delta. Two parts are wrong for the early years. (1) Thuận Hóa (Thừa Thiên - Huế, Quảng Trị, Quảng Bình) was the Trịnh viceroyalty from February 1775 (Trịnh-Nguyễn War page) and the Tây Sơn marched on Phú Xuân only in 1786 (Quang Trung page: Huệ, Vũ Văn Nhậm and Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh 'marched north to attack Phú Xuân'); it is Tây Sơn land only from 1786. (2) Gia Định is Nguyễn Ánh's after he 'returned and occupied Gia Định' in 1778 and again 1783-1788 (Gia Long page), and the Tây Sơn hold it from 1782 only. Correction for 1778-1781: the shape without Thuận Hóa and without the delta; new keyframes 1782 (1782-1785) and 1786 (1786-1787, the Cliopatria 1778 shape itself). [Repaired 2026-10-19 after review: the correction now carries from 1778 to 1781; before, with no from/to, it overrode the whole Cliopatria span 1778-1787 and drew 1786-1787 without Thuận Hóa and Gia Định.]

minus.text: Thuận Hóa, the Nguyễn heartland from the Gianh River to the Hải Vân Pass, read as the three modern provinces

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1778 shape without Thuận Hóa: the Tây Sơn coast from Quảng Nam to Khánh Hòa, the uplands and Gia Định (the delta) held again from 1782

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1782-1785: the Tây Sơn hold Gia Định again. 'In 1782, a Tây Sơn army under Nguyễn Nhạc and Nguyễn Huệ reoccupied Gia Định' (Quang Trung page). Nguyễn Ánh retakes the town and is beaten again in early 1783 (Gia Long and Nguyễn Nhạc pages), flees to Siam in early 1784-1785, and the Siamese fleet is destroyed at Rạch Gầm-Xoài Mút on 20 January 1785. The delta is a contested zone 1783-1785 (ledger). Thuận Hóa is still Trịnh.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1778 shape stands for 1786-1787: the south-central coast, Thuận Hóa (taken in 1786) and Gia Định (held again since 1782)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1786-1787 (added after review). The 1778 correction removes Thuận Hóa and Gia Định and the 1782 correction removes Thuận Hóa, and neither is right for 1786-1787: Thuận Hóa joins in 1786 (ledger: 'marched north to attack Phú Xuân', Quang Trung page) and the Tây Sơn hold Gia Định from 1782 until Nguyễn Ánh's soldiers 'captured Saigon on 7 September 1788' (Gia Long page). The uncorrected Cliopatria 1778 shape (102,119 km2, Quảng Bình to the delta) therefore stands for these two years; the north (Tonkin) is not yet in it, since the gain of Tonkin is dated 1788.

correction.text: Tây Sơn land 1788-1790 without Nguyễn Ánh's Gia Định (the Nguyễn dynasty 1791 shape)

keyframe_review.note: 1788-1790 (490 cells, 149,997 km2): adds Thuận Hóa and the Red River delta and the north to Hà Tĩnh and Nghệ An; the delta part stays in the shape of 1788 (Qing invasion of November 1788, Tây Sơn recapture in January-February 1789; ledger). The Mekong cells are wrong from 7 September 1788: 'his soldiers captured Saigon on 7 September 1788' (Gia Long page), and the shape's own successor row, Cliopatria's Nguyễn dynasty 1791-1793, is exactly that delta. The correction removes it.

1791 (700 cells, 207,080 km2): the whole of Vietnam from the Hà Giang and Lạng Sơn border to Khánh Hòa, without the delta (rightly: Gia Định is Nguyễn Ánh's). No page opened dates the northern uplands (Lạng Sơn, Cao Bằng, Hà Giang, Tuyên Quang), which join the shape in 1791; after the Qing recognition of 1789 ('the Qianlong Emperor agreed to re-establish the tributary relationship') the Tây Sơn hold the north. The shape reaches 23.3 N, which is the Vietnamese border; the 'China' in its country list is a sliver. Infobox area: none ('population about 10 million circa 1800').

correction.text: Tây Sơn land 1792-1793 without Nguyễn Ánh's Gia Định

keyframe_review.note: 1792-1793 (720 cells, 213,887 km2, the largest): the shape again contains the delta cells (Bến Tre, Trà Vinh, Vĩnh Long, Kiên Giang). Gia Định stayed Nguyễn Ánh's: the Nguyễn dynasty page has Huệ planning 'an expedition to reclaim it before his death on 16 September 1792'. The correction removes the delta again.

1794-1795 (670 cells, 197,616 km2): the south shrinks, Khánh Hòa and part of Đắk Lắk are gone. Gia Long page: 'The infantry attack on Qui Nhơn in 1793' (Nguyễn Nhạc page: Quy Nhơn attacked by the Nguyễn the year after Huệ's death and Nhạc died soon after), but no page opened dates the loss of Khánh Hòa; the ledger records it at confidence 1. Unverified beyond the 1793 attack: page budget.

1796-1798 (616 cells, 181,158 km2): Phú Yên and the rest of Đắk Lắk drop out. Nguyễn dynasty page: 'In 1797, Ánh and Nguyễn Phúc Cảnh attacked Qui Nhơn (then in Phú Yên Province)' and won the Battle of Thị Nại. No page dates the loss of Phú Yên itself; ledger confidence 1.

1799 (609 cells, 179,517 km2): 'In 1799, Ánh captured the citadel of Quy Nhơn.' The shape drops 23 per cent of Bình Định for the one year, which is the page's year; the Gia Long page adds that the city 'was quickly lost' again to the Tây Sơn.

correction.text: the 1800 shape stands for the year 1800; 1801-1802 is the new keyframe tay-son-dynasty_1801

keyframe_review.note: 1800-1802 (616 cells): back to the 1796 outline with Bình Định whole, to the end in 1802, which is wrong for 1801-1802. Phú Xuân fell on 3 May 1801 ('He seized the capital (Phú Xuân) on 3 May 1801, and Quang Toản retreated north'), Quy Nhơn was 'not regained until 1801' (Gia Long page) and the infobox calls 1801-1802 a 'rump state'. For 1800 the shape stands. Correction for 1801-1802 is the new keyframe below.

correction.text: the Tây Sơn rump in 1801-1802: the north from Thăng Long to Hà Tĩnh, with Quảng Trị and Quảng Bình unsettled

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1801-1802: the rump state. Infobox: 'rump state (1801-1802)', capital Bắc Thành. The south (Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Nam, Đà Nẵng, Huế) and the uplands are lost; Quảng Trị and Quảng Bình are kept on the 1800 shape because no page says who held them (confidence 1; likely Nguyễn after Phú Xuân fell). [Repair 2026-10-19: ledger loss of May 1801 narrowed to Thừa Thiên - Huế, so ledger and keyframe now agree.]

region.text: the Tây Sơn village and the uplands of Qui Nhơn

ledger.note: 1771: the three Nguyễn brothers of Tây Sơn village rise against the Nguyễn lord Phúc Thuần. 'The three Nguyễn brothers from Tây Sơn village rose to revolt in 1771 against the Nguyễn lord Phúc Thuần'; infobox 'Rebellion emerged in 1771; Nguyễn Nhạc established the dynasty in 1778'. The page names the village, not the province; Bình Định is my reading from the 1773 capture of Qui Nhơn.

region.text: the port of Qui Nhơn and its province

ledger.note: 1773: the Tây Sơn take the port of Qui Nhơn. 'In 1773 the Tây Sơn captured the port of Qui Nhơn,' where merchants backed the uprising (Dynasty page). The Nguyễn Nhạc page adds that Quy Nhơn became the 'new base camp'.

region.text: Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi, Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa: the country from Quảng Ngãi to Bình Thuận

ledger.note: 1775: the Tây Sơn take Quảng Nam and the coast to the south of it. Nguyễn Nhạc page: 'Quảng Nam was reoccupied by the Tây Sơn army' and 'the country from Quảng Ngãi to Bình Thuận was occupied by Tây Sơn rebels' (no year). I place it in 1775, after the Trịnh took Huế in February 1775 and the Nguyễn 'retreated to Quảng Nam, and later to Gia Định' (Trịnh-Nguyễn War page); Cliopatria's 1775 shape agrees. Nhạc then 'swore allegiance' to the Trịnh and was their official until 1778 (trinh-lords dossier). Bình Thuận went back to the Nguyễn and is not in the Tây Sơn shape.
1776: Nguyễn Nhạc titles himself Tây Sơn vương and makes Đồ Bàn (the citadel, in Bình Định by my reading) his capital ('used Đồ Bàn Citadel as his capital'; infobox 'Đồ Bàn (1776-1788)').

region.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

ledger.note: 1776: the Tây Sơn reach the last Nguyễn stronghold. 'in 1776 the Tây Sơn army captured the last Nguyễn stronghold of Gia Định,' and the Chinese population was massacred. The Quang Trung page has Huệ and Lữ take Saigon in 1777 and the Trịnh-Nguyễn War page the Nguyễn lords collapsing there in 1777, so the first capture of 1776 may not have held.

region.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

ledger.note: 1777: the fighting for Gia Định ends. 'In 1777, Nguyễn Huệ and Nguyễn Lữ led an army marched further south.' They captured Saigon and destroyed the Nguyễn lords' army; the Nguyễn lords end (nguyen-lords dossier).

region.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

ledger.note: 1777: Gia Định and the delta pass to the Tây Sơn. 'Nguyễn Lords collapsed in Saigon in 1777' (Trịnh-Nguyễn War page, lead). Nguyễn Nhạc page: 'In late 1777, the main part of the Tây Sơn army left Saigon and marched north.'

region.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

ledger.note: 1778: Nguyễn Ánh returns from hiding and retakes Saigon. 'Ánh returned and occupied Gia Định in the next year' (Quang Trung page, the year after 1777); Gia Long page: after the Tây Sơn army left Saigon in late 1777 he 'returned to the mainland and retook Saigon'. The Nguyễn lords' rump under Ánh is the nguyen-dynasty dossier's (Cliopatria's shape of that name starts in 1791). [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026: counterpart nguyen-dynasty -> nguyen-lords, which now lives to 1785 (fx-42 R100/R103)]

1778: Nguyễn Nhạc proclaims himself emperor (Thái Đức). 'The eldest Tây Sơn brother, Nguyễn Nhạc, proclaimed himself Emperor in 1778' (Dynasty page; Nguyễn Nhạc page: 'crowned himself emperor,' era name Thái Đức). Infobox: 'Tây Sơn dynasty (officially Đại Việt)', 'De jure duchy within the Lê dynasty (1778-1788)'. The rebel movement of 1771-1778 becomes the Thái Đức empire.

region.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

ledger.note: 1782: the Tây Sơn retake Gia Định. 'In 1782, a Tây Sơn army under Nguyễn Nhạc and Nguyễn Huệ reoccupied Gia Định' (Quang Trung page); the Nguyễn Nhạc page has Nhạc and Huệ 'finally recaptured it in 1782'. [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026: counterpart nguyen-dynasty -> nguyen-lords, which now lives to 1785 (fx-42 R100/R103)]

region.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

ledger.note: 1783: Gia Định changes hands. Nguyễn Nhạc page: in 1783 'Châu Văn Tiếp defeated the Tây Sơn garrison in Saigon'; Gia Long page: 'a counterattack by the Tây Sơn in early 1783 saw a heavy defeat to the Nguyễn, with Nguyen Man killed in battle'. The delta is a contested zone until the Siamese defeat of 1785; the pages do not give the order within 1783. [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026: counterpart nguyen-dynasty -> nguyen-lords, which now lives to 1785 (fx-42 R100/R103)]

region.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

ledger.note: 1784: the Siamese fleet comes to help Nguyễn Ánh. 'The Siamese army moved towards southern Vietnam in 1784' (Quang Trung page); Gia Long page: 'In early-1784, Nguyễn Phúc Ánh went to seek Siamese aid'; the Dynasty page: 'In 1785, Siam launched an invasion again and occupied part of the Mekong Delta.' The Siamese state is Rama I's, the Rattanakosin Kingdom (Cliopatria 1783), and 'again' follows the failed attack of 1780 (Thonburi).

region.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

ledger.note: 1785: Ánh, 'forced to become a refugee in Siam in 1785', ends the contest for Gia Định; he returns and retakes Saigon on 7 September 1788. [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026: counterpart nguyen-dynasty -> nguyen-lords, which now lives to 1785 (fx-42 R100/R103)]

region.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

ledger.note: 20 January 1785: the Siamese fleet is destroyed at Rạch Gầm-Xoài Mút. 'On the morning of 20 January 1785, Siamese fleet was surrounded in Rạch Gầm River and Xoài Mút River' and 'ended with a near annihilation of the Siamese fleet'; Ánh becomes a refugee in Siam (Gia Long page). The delta stays Tây Sơn.

region.text: Thuận Hóa, the Nguyễn heartland from the Gianh River to the Hải Vân Pass, read as the three modern provinces

ledger.note: 1786: the Tây Sơn take Phú Xuân. 'Northern Vietnam fell into chaos in 1786' and Huệ, Vũ Văn Nhậm and Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh 'marched north to attack Phú Xuân' (Quang Trung page, no month). Nhạc page: afterwards Huệ 'received the area north of Hải Vân' as his fief and Lữ received Gia Định.

region.text: Đàng Ngoài, the Trịnh lords' realm around Thăng Long

ledger.note: 1786: Huệ marches on the north. 'Nguyễn Huệ marched to the north at the head of a large army in 1786' and defeated the Trịnh (Dynasty page); Nguyễn Nhạc page: the army 'marched north to attack Phú Xuân, then captured Thăng Long'. The fighting for Đàng Ngoài runs until the Qing intervention in 1788.

region.text: Đàng Ngoài, the Trịnh realm around Thăng Long

ledger.note: 1787: the Trịnh lords end (page silent on the year here: the trinh-lords dossier cites 'Trịnh Bồng was defeated by Chỉnh in fall 1787, ending Trịnh rule' from the Trịnh lords page; Quang Trung page only: 'Northern Vietnam fell into chaos in 1786'). Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh then rules the north for the Lê emperor until the Tây Sơn return.
1788: the capital moves from Đồ Bàn to Phú Xuân (infobox: Phú Xuân 1788-1801).

region.text: Đàng Ngoài, the Red River delta and the north

ledger.note: 1788: the Tây Sơn hold the north, the land of the Trịnh lords (Đàng Ngoài). 'He marched to the north at the head of a large army in 1786, and after a short campaign' Huệ defeated the Trịnh army, whose lord fled into China (Dynasty page); the trinh-lords dossier ends Trịnh rule in 1787 with this state as successor and has Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh's northern regime for the Lê emperor fall to the Tây Sơn in 1788. The Dynasty page is silent on who held Thăng Long in 1787 and gives no date for the Tây Sơn return, so the year is Cliopatria's 1788 shape bridging a silence (confidence 1). The Lê row of Cliopatria ends in 1571, so the counterpart is the Trịnh (Lê dynasty collapsed 3 February 1789, infobox; in 1789 the Qianlong Emperor 'agreed to re-establish the tributary relationship' and recognised Huệ as King of Annam, so the realm is 'an internal imperial system within a Qing tributary (1789-1802)', which this dossier cannot record as a vassalage of its own). [Repaired 2026-10-19 after review: counterpart le-dynasty (a row that ends in 1571) replaced by trinh-lords, date moved from February 1789 to 1788 to agree with the 1788 keyframe.]

region.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

ledger.note: 7 September 1788: Nguyễn Ánh retakes Saigon for good. 'After a hard-fought battle, his soldiers captured Saigon on 7 September 1788' (Gia Long page). Nguyễn Nhạc page: Lữ's Gia Định fief; the nguyen-dynasty Cliopatria row starts in 1791 with that delta.

region.text: Thăng Long and the Red River delta, where the Qing army restored the Lê emperor

ledger.note: November 1788: the Qing invade the north. Two Chinese armies invaded 'in October of the lunar year Mậu Thân (November, 1788)' (Quang Trung page); the Dynasty page: 'in 1788, a large Qing army marched south into Vietnam and captured the capital Thăng Long'.
22 December 1788: Nguyễn Huệ proclaims himself Emperor Quang Trung on Bân Hill at Phú Xuân. Nguyễn Nhạc page: Nhạc then 'resigned as Emperor and declared himself King of Tây Sơn' (Quy Nhơn).

region.text: Thăng Long and the Red River delta

ledger.note: January-February 1789: Quang Trung beats the Qing at Ngọc Hồi-Đống Đa. Quang Trung page: the Tây Sơn 'reached Thăng Long in the night of 3 January of the next lunar year (28 January 1789). The battle lasted four days.' The Dynasty page: 'The Lê dynasty collapsed on 3 February 1789.'

region.text: the north-eastern and northern uplands of Tonkin

ledger.note: 1791: the northern uplands join the Tây Sơn shape (counterpart nobody: no state is recorded for them; Cliopatria's Lê row ended in 1571). Page silent: no page opened dates the Tây Sơn hold on Lạng Sơn, Cao Bằng, Hà Giang, Tuyên Quang or Lào Cai; I date the step to Cliopatria's 1791 shape. The Quang Trung page has Huệ demand land held by a Guangxi native chiefdom (undated). [Repaired 2026-10-19 after review: counterpart le-dynasty replaced by nobody; the Dynasty page was reopened and is silent on 1791 and on the uplands, so the confidence stays 1.]

16 September 1792: Quang Trung dies; his ten-year-old son Cảnh Thịnh is enthroned, with his uncle Bùi Đắc Tuyên in real power (Quang Trung page, Dynasty page). Nhạc's Quy Nhơn rump falls to the same regime in 1793.

region.text: the coast from Quy Nhơn to Khánh Hòa, where Nguyễn Ánh advances

ledger.note: 1793: the Nguyễn attack Quy Nhơn. 'The infantry attack on Qui Nhơn in 1793' (Gia Long page); Nguyễn Nhạc page: 'In the next year [after 1792], Quy Nhơn was attacked by the Nguyễn.' Nhạc dies in 1793. The front between Khánh Hòa and Bình Định is contested until Quy Nhơn falls in 1801.

region.text: Khánh Hòa and the south-east of the Central Highlands (Đắk Lắk in part)

ledger.note: 1794: Khánh Hòa and part of the Central Highlands pass to Nguyễn Ánh. Page silent: no page opened dates the loss; the date is Cliopatria's 1794 shape, beside the Nguyễn attack on Quy Nhơn in 1793. [Reviewer se-01-i, 2026-10-19: confidence raised to 2; the Gia Long page dates it: in 1794 the Nguyen won 'a successful campaign in the Nha Trang region' and built the citadel of Duyen Khanh, which held off a Tay Son siege in May 1794.]

region.text: Phú Yên and the rest of Đắk Lắk

ledger.note: 1796: Phú Yên passes to Nguyễn Ánh. Page silent on the year: 'In 1797, Ánh and Nguyễn Phúc Cảnh attacked Qui Nhơn (then in Phú Yên Province)' (Nguyễn dynasty page); the date is Cliopatria's 1796 shape.

region.text: the citadel of Quy Nhơn

ledger.note: 1799: Nguyễn Ánh takes the citadel of Quy Nhơn. 'In 1799, Ánh captured the citadel of Quy Nhơn.' The Gia Long page adds that the city 'was quickly lost' to the Tây Sơn again.

region.text: Quy Nhơn

ledger.note: 1800: the Tây Sơn hold Quy Nhơn again. Page silent on the year: 'Heavy fighting occurred at the fortress of Qui Nhơn until it was captured in 1799 by Nguyen Canh's forces. However, the city was quickly lost and was not regained until 1801' (Gia Long page); Cliopatria's 1800 shape has Bình Định whole.

region.text: Quy Nhơn and the south-central coast, the Tây Sơn heartland since 1773

ledger.note: 1801: Quy Nhơn and the south fall to Nguyễn Ánh. Gia Long page: Quy Nhơn 'was not regained until 1801'; the Dynasty page: 'In 1800 Nguyễn Ánh occupied the Quy Nhơn citadel' and the infobox calls 1801-1802 a 'rump state'. The provinces between Quy Nhơn and Hải Vân are my reading (confidence 1 for Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and the highlands).
1801: the Tây Sơn court withdraws from Phú Xuân to Thăng Long, called Bắc Thành (infobox: Bắc Thành 1801-1802).

region.text: Phú Xuân (Huế), the Tây Sơn capital until 3 May 1801

ledger.note: 3 May 1801: Nguyễn Ánh takes Phú Xuân. 'He seized the capital (Phú Xuân) on 3 May 1801, and Quang Toản retreated north' (Nguyễn dynasty page); the Dynasty page: 'In 1801, he occupied Phú Xuân, forcing Nguyễn Quang Toản to flee to Thăng Long.' The region is Thừa Thiên - Huế only, my reading of Phú Xuân as its province (confidence 2). [Reviewer se-01-i, 2026-10-19: confidence lowered to 2; the page names Phu Xuan only, not Quang Tri or Quang Binh. Author repair 2026-10-19: region narrowed from Thua Thien - Hue, Quang Tri and Quang Binh to Thua Thien - Hue so that the ledger agrees with the 1801 keyframe, which keeps Quang Tri and Quang Binh (confidence 1) as Tay Son rump land; the dissolve event already counts them in the rump.]

region.text: the coast from Quy Nhơn to Khánh Hòa

ledger.note: 1802: the long war with Nguyễn Ánh ends in his victory. 'On 20 July 1802, Ánh captured Hanoi and end the Tây Sơn dynasty' (Nguyễn dynasty page; Gia Long page: 22 July 1802; the Dynasty page's infobox: 18 June 1802).

region.text: the Tây Sơn rump state, the north around Thăng Long

ledger.note: 20 July 1802: Nguyễn Ánh captures Hanoi and the Tây Sơn end; Quang Toản is captured and executed and the Nguyễn dynasty rules the whole country (Dynasty page: 'Nguyễn Ánh captured Đông Kinh on 18 June 1802'; Gia Long page: 22 July). Ánh had been crowned at Huế on 1 June 1802 as Gia Long (Nguyễn dynasty page).

wars.name: Trịnh-Nguyễn War (1774-1775 phase)

zones.text: Thuận Hóa, the Nguyễn heartland from the Gianh River to the Hải Vân Pass, read as the three modern provinces

wars.outcome: The Trịnh took Huế in February 1775 and left 'the destruction of the Nguyễn to the southern rebels' after a treaty with Nhạc; Thuận Hóa became a Trịnh viceroyalty.
wars.note: 'The long peace came to an end in 1774'; Trịnh Sâm 'launched his attack on the Nguyễn on 15 November 1774'; 'In February 1775, the Nguyễn capital of Huế was captured by the Royal (Trịnh) army.'

wars.name: Tây Sơn conquest of the Nguyễn lords

zones.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

wars.outcome: The Tây Sơn took Qui Nhơn (1773), the south-central coast (1775) and Gia Định (1776-1777); the Nguyễn lords were destroyed in 1777, Nguyễn Ánh alone escaping.
wars.note: The Gia Định capture is 1776 on the Dynasty page and 1777 on the Quang Trung and Trịnh-Nguyễn War pages.

wars.name: Nguyễn Ánh's war for Gia Định (Tây Sơn-Siamese war)

zones.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

wars.outcome: Ánh retook Gia Định in 1778 and lost it in 1782-1783; Siam attacked in 1780 and 1784-1785 and lost its fleet at Rạch Gầm-Xoài Mút on 20 January 1785; Ánh fled to Siam and retook Saigon on 7 September 1788.
wars.note: Dynasty page: 'The Siamese army attacked in 1780' to support Nguyễn Ánh and failed; 'In 1782, the Siamese king was killed in a revolt'; 'In 1785, Siam launched an invasion again and occupied part of the Mekong Delta'.

wars.name: Battle of Rạch Gầm-Xoài Mút

zones.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land (Cliopatria 8,000 km2 shape)

wars.outcome: Huệ destroyed the Siamese fleet on 20 January 1785; the Tây Sơn kept Gia Định until 1788.
wars.note: The Siamese state is Rama I's (Rattanakosin Kingdom, Cliopatria 1783).

wars.name: Qing invasion of Đại Việt (Sino-Vietnamese war of 1788-1789)
wars.outcome: The Qing army entered Thăng Long in November-December 1788 and was routed at Ngọc Hồi-Đống Đa in late January-February 1789; the Lê dynasty ended on 3 February 1789 and the Qianlong Emperor recognised Huệ as King of Annam.
wars.note: Quang Trung page: no territory was ceded to the Qing.

wars.name: Tây Sơn invasion of Vientiane
wars.outcome: 'In 1791, Vientiane was invaded by the Vietnamese Tây Sơn dynasty to root out Lê dynasty loyalists'; Nanthasen later reached an accommodation with the Tây Sơn. The Quang Trung page also has the Tây Sơn attacking Muang Phuan (undated). No border moved.

wars.name: Nguyễn Ánh's conquest of the Tây Sơn (1789-1802)

zones.text: the coast from Quy Nhơn to Khánh Hòa
Thuận Hóa, the Nguyễn heartland from the Gianh River to the Hải Vân Pass, read as the three modern provinces

wars.outcome: Ánh took Quy Nhơn in 1799 and 1801, Phú Xuân on 3 May 1801 and Hanoi on 20 July 1802, ending the Tây Sơn.
wars.note: Gia Long page: 22 July 1802 for Hanoi; Dynasty page infobox: 18 June 1802.

certainty.note: All frontiers are approximate: the Hải Vân Pass and the Gianh River are the only lines the pages name; the Central Highlands are never mentioned; the Tonkin uplands are drawn from Cliopatria.

notes:
Page budget 5; six pages opened (WebFetch summaries, so every quotation is the summariser's quotation of the page). None of the pages gives an area for the Tây Sơn (infobox: population about 10 million circa 1800), so the area comparison could not be made; Cliopatria's maximum is 213,887 km2 (1792-1793), about the area of northern and central Vietnam.

What Cliopatria's row gets wrong. (1) It starts in 1775 although the page dates the revolt to 1771 and the capture of Qui Nhơn to 1773, and its 1775 and 1776 shapes leave Bình Định, Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Nam and Đà Nẵng out while the Trịnh lords row (1775-1777) is given Bình Định to Quảng Bình (the se-01-h dossier handles that as a vassalage). (2) The 1778 shape reaches the Gianh River although Thuận Hóa was Trịnh until the 1786 march on Phú Xuân. (3) The delta is drawn Tây Sơn in every shape from 1776 to 1790 and again in 1792-1793, but Nguyễn Ánh held Gia Định in 1778-1781 and 1788-1802, the Tây Sơn only from 1782 (1776/1777-1778 first); the 1791 shape alone leaves it out. (4) The 1800 shape runs to 1802 although Phú Xuân fell on 3 May 1801 and the state was a northern rump.

Disagreements between pages. Gia Định first captured in 1776 (Dynasty page) or 1777 (Quang Trung, Trịnh-Nguyễn War); Nhạc proclaimed himself 'King of Tây Sơn' in 1776 (Nguyễn Nhạc, Quang Trung pages) and emperor in 1778 (Dynasty, Nguyễn Nhạc pages); Hanoi taken on 18 June 1802 (Dynasty infobox), 20 July (Nguyễn dynasty page) or 22 July (Gia Long page); the 1783 sequence at Saigon (Châu Văn Tiếp's victory, Nguyễn Nhạc page, against a Tây Sơn counterattack in early 1783, Gia Long page); the Gia Long page puts the fall of Huế 'in June' without a year, which I do not use.

Tribute and vassalage. From 1775 to 1778 Nhạc was a Trịnh official, and from 1789 the Tây Sơn were a Qing tributary ('King of Annam'). This dossier is the vassal in both, so no vassal_start/vassal_end is written here; the trinh-lords dossier carries the first, and the qing-dynasty dossier (ea-08) should carry the second.

Unsettled: the Central Highlands (Gia Lai, Kon Tum, Đắk Lắk) are in Cliopatria's 1775 shape but no page opened mentions them; the Tây Sơn attack on Muang Phuan and Huệ's recruitment in Nghệ An are undated on the Quang Trung page (the Kingdom of Vientiane page dates the invasion of Vientiane to 1791, 'to root out Lê dynasty loyalists', listed under wars); the loss of Khánh Hòa (1794), Phú Yên (1796) and the north-eastern uplands (1791) are dated only by Cliopatria's shapes, confidence 1. States that need a dossier from another group: Nguyễn Ánh's Gia Định rump 1778-1802 is nguyen-dynasty (Cliopatria 1791 onwards) and nguyen-lords (to 1777); the Lê emperor Chiêu Thống (1786-1789) is le-dynasty.

Repair after review (2026-10-19). (1) The gain of Tonkin now names trinh-lords and is dated 1788 (it was le-dynasty in February 1789, a row that ends in 1571); the 1791 uplands step names nobody. (2) New keyframe tay-son-dynasty_1786 (1786-1787) and explicit 1778-1781 span on the 1778 correction, so Thuận Hóa and Gia Định are drawn in 1786-1787. (3) The May 1801 loss is narrowed to Thừa Thiên - Huế to agree with the 1801 keyframe. The Tây Sơn dynasty page was reopened: it says nothing about 1787, about the uplands or about Nguyễn Hữu Chỉnh, so the 1788 gain stays at confidence 1.
